title: Flux, GitOps & Argo CD — Interview Questions

questions.question: What is FluxCD?
options: A push-based CI server that applies manifests to clusters
An open source continuous delivery tool for Kubernetes that follows GitOps
A container registry for storing Helm charts
A monitoring and alerting stack for Kubernetes

questions.question: What does pull-based deployment mean?
options: The cluster pulls its desired state instead of a CI server pushing changes in
The CI server pushes manifests to the cluster with cluster-admin credentials
Kubelets pull container images from a registry
Developers run kubectl apply from their laptops

questions.question: What is the GitOps Toolkit?
options: A CLI plugin that generates Helm charts
A hosted dashboard for Flux resources
The set of specialised controllers and APIs that make up Flux v2
A drop-in replacement for Kustomize

questions.question: What is a GitRepository object?
options: A Helm chart repository definition
A notification-controller resource for webhooks
A kustomize-controller resource that applies a path
A source-controller resource declaring which Git URL and revision to fetch, how often, and which secret holds credentials

questions.question: What is a Flux Kustomization, and how is it different from a kustomization.yaml file?
options: They are the same thing under different names
A Flux Kustomization is a cluster object pointing at a path inside a source artifact; kustomization.yaml is the Kustomize configuration inside that path
A Flux Kustomization replaces Kustomize entirely
kustomization.yaml is the cluster object; Flux Kustomization is only a CLI concept

questions.question: What does the interval field do?
options: It sets how often the controller reconciles the object
It sets a hard timeout after which the object is deleted
It sets the retention period of source artifacts
It sets the delay before the first reconciliation only

questions.question: What does prune: true do?
options: Deletes the Git commit after it has been applied
Prevents Flux from ever deleting anything in the cluster
Enables garbage collection: objects whose manifests were removed from Git are deleted on the next reconciliation
Prunes old container images from nodes

questions.question: How do you install Flux on a cluster?
options: kubectl apply -f flux.yaml
flux bootstrap, after running flux check --pre
helm install flux fluxcd/flux
flux create cluster --managed

questions.question: Which command shows the status of all Kustomizations?
options: flux get kustomizations (or flux get ks)
flux status all
kubectl get flux
flux list resources

questions.question: How do you force Flux to sync now instead of waiting for the interval?
options: flux sync kustomization <name>
flux reset kustomization <name>
kubectl rollout restart kustomization <name>
flux reconcile kustomization <name> --with-source

questions.question: Does Flux have a web UI?
options: Yes, a full UI ships with Flux
No — Flux has no UI of its own, though several ecosystem UIs can display Flux resources
Yes, but only for Helm releases
Only in the enterprise edition

questions.question: How is Flux different from Argo CD at a high level?
options: Argo CD is a set of composable controllers; Flux is a monolith with a UI
Flux ships a UI while Argo CD does not
Argo CD centres on an Application resource with its own UI, RBAC and SSO; Flux is composable controllers using Kubernetes RBAC with no bundled UI
They are identical in architecture and interfaces

questions.question: What is a HelmRelease?
options: A helm-controller resource declaring a chart, its version or range, values and lifecycle settings
A Helm chart repository index
A Kustomize overlay for Helm values
A cluster-wide Helm binary installation

questions.question: How do you pass different Helm values per environment?
options: Duplicate the whole HelmRelease per environment with copy-paste
Patch spec.values with Kustomize overlays per environment, or use valuesFrom to read per-cluster ConfigMaps or Secrets
Set environment variables on helm-controller
A HelmRelease can only ever have one set of values

questions.question: How does helm-controller handle a failed upgrade?
options: It ignores failures and retries forever
You must delete the HelmRelease and recreate it manually
Failures are only reported to chat, never acted on
You configure spec.upgrade.remediation (retries, rollback on failure), and spec.install.remediation for installs

questions.question: What is drift detection in HelmRelease?
options: It detects Git commits that were not signed
It detects drift between two branches in Git
Helm-controller compares live cluster objects with the release manifest and reports or corrects differences, configured via spec.driftDetection
It compares container images between registries

questions.question: What is an OCIRepository and why use it?
options: A source that pulls an artifact from an OCI registry instead of Git, decoupling clusters from Git access
A mirror of a GitRepository inside a registry namespace
A HelmRepository limited to private registries
A secret store for registry credentials

questions.question: How do you order deployments, for example CRDs before the apps that use them?
options: Put them in the same Kustomization; Kubernetes sorts it out
Use spec.postBuild.substitute to add ordering labels
Order them with flux suspend and flux resume
Split them into separate Kustomizations and use spec.dependsOn on the dependent one

questions.question: What are health checks in a Kustomization?
options: spec.wait: true waits for all applied resources to become ready, spec.healthChecks lists specific objects, and spec.timeout marks the Kustomization failed
Health checks are only available in HelmRelease
Health checks require a Prometheus server
spec.wait only waits for pods to be scheduled

questions.question: How do you manage secrets in a Flux repository?
options: Commit plain Secrets and restrict repository access
Store secrets in a ConfigMap
Let developers apply secrets manually with kubectl
Encrypt Secret manifests with SOPS (age or cloud KMS) and set spec.decryption.provider: sops on the Kustomization

questions.question: What is post-build variable substitution?
options: It rewrites Kubernetes API versions after the build
It builds manifests before Kustomize runs
It replaces ${VAR} placeholders after the Kustomize build using spec.postBuild.substitute or substituteFrom
It substitutes container image tags in Git

questions.question: How does image update automation work?
options: ImageRepository scans tags, ImagePolicy picks the newest by rule, and ImageUpdateAutomation rewrites manifests at marker comments and commits
ImageRepository edits Git directly on every new tag
Flux patches the running Deployment directly in the cluster
Image automation only works with plain Helm charts

questions.question: How do you send Flux events to Slack or Teams?
options: Add a Slack URL annotation to every Kustomization
Create an Alert that references a Provider holding the chat type and a secret with the webhook or token
Install a Slack plugin inside kustomize-controller
notification-controller posts to Slack by default

questions.question: What is a Receiver?
options: A resource that receives Git pushes and deletes old commits
A proxy that caches source artifacts
A notification-controller resource exposing a webhook endpoint that triggers immediate reconciliation
A receiver of Helm chart events inside the cluster

questions.question: How do you pause Flux for a resource during maintenance?
options: flux suspend kustomization <name>, then flux resume kustomization <name>
flux pause kustomization <name>
Scale the controller Deployment to zero
Delete the Kustomization and re-add it later

questions.question: How do you preview what a change will do before merging?
options: flux preview kustomization <name>
flux build --dry-run=server
kubectl diff -f .
flux diff kustomization <name> --path ./local/path

questions.question: How do you find which Flux object manages a given Deployment?
options: flux trace on the object, or the kustomize.toolkit.fluxcd.io/name and namespace labels
kubectl get deployment -o yaml shows the Git commit
flux get all --managed-by
Only by searching the repository by hand

questions.question: What happens if someone edits a Flux-managed object with kubectl?
options: The edit persists until the next Flux upgrade
Flux stops reconciling that object permanently
Flux commits the manual change back to Git
On the next reconciliation kustomize-controller re-applies the Git state and the manual change is overwritten

questions.question: How does Flux authenticate to a private Git repository?
options: With a Secret referenced by spec.secretRef on the GitRepository, holding SSH keys and known hosts or HTTPS credentials
With cluster-admin credentials in the controller environment
With a personal access token in plaintext in the GitRepository spec
Flux cannot access private repositories

questions.question: How do you upgrade Flux itself?
options: Delete and reinstall the controllers by hand
Flux upgrades itself with no action required
Upgrade the CLI, then rerun flux bootstrap with the same arguments so Flux updates itself through Git
Run helm upgrade flux on each cluster

questions.question: How would you lay out a Git repository for many clusters?
options: A clusters/ directory with one folder per cluster, infrastructure/ for shared controllers and CRDs, and apps/ with base and per-environment overlays
A branches/ directory with one branch per cluster
One repository per Kustomization
A single flat folder with every manifest

questions.question: How do you implement multi-tenancy with Flux?
options: One shared namespace for all tenants with full RBAC
Tenants get cluster-admin and are trusted
Multi-tenancy is not possible with Flux
A namespace and limited service account per tenant, set via spec.serviceAccountName so Flux impersonates it

questions.question: How do you promote a release from staging to production?
options: Rerun flux bootstrap for production
A pull request bumping the version in the production overlay, OCI artifacts promoted by retagging, or image policies with per-environment tag patterns
Promotion is only possible by copying YAML by hand
Edit the live Deployment in production

questions.question: How do you monitor Flux at scale?
options: kubectl logs the controllers and read them daily
Flux ships a built-in monitoring UI
Prometheus metrics plus the published example Grafana dashboards; alert on not-Ready resources, reconciliation duration and suspended objects
Only Argo CD can be monitored

questions.question: How do you secure the supply chain in a Flux setup?
options: Sign OCI artifacts and images in CI (for example with Cosign) and configure OCIRepository verification so Flux only applies signed content
Trust every artifact that arrives from the registry
Disable pruning to protect the cluster
Give every developer cluster-admin

questions.question: How do you handle CRD and controller upgrades safely?
options: Delete all CRDs and recreate them after the upgrade
Upgrade controllers and CRDs at the same time in production
Keep CRDs in their own Kustomization that other layers depend on, test in staging, use HelmRelease CRD policies deliberately and be careful with pruning CRDs
Always set prune: true on CRDs to keep them clean

questions.question: How would you bootstrap hundreds of clusters consistently?
options: Run bootstrap by hand on each cluster with slightly different folders
Automate cluster creation with IaC, run bootstrap during provisioning and template the cluster folder so the folder is the only per-cluster difference
Use one shared Kustomization for every cluster
Skip bootstrap and apply manifests with kubectl

questions.question: What are the risks of image update automation in production?
options: None — image automation is always safe in production
It only affects staging clusters by design
It removes the need for Git entirely
The bot needs write credentials and an unexpected tag can roll out without review; limit it to staging or strict semver patch ranges and require PRs plus signature verification

questions.question: How do you reduce reconciliation load on a large cluster?
options: Set every interval to 10 seconds
Use sensible intervals, trigger syncs with Receivers instead of short polling, split very large Kustomizations and tune controller concurrency
Disable health checks
Put every resource in one giant Kustomization

questions.question: When would you choose Flux over Argo CD, or the other way round?
options: Flux is strictly better in every case
Argo CD has no UI
Both tools require a UI to work

Flux fits teams wanting everything as Kubernetes resources, native RBAC, OCI-based delivery and composable controllers; Argo CD fits teams wanting a built-in developer UI, application-centric views and its own SSO/RBAC

questions.question: A Kustomization shows “Ready False” with a build error. What do you check?
options: Read the message with flux get ks <name> and flux events --for Kustomization/<name>; look for invalid YAML, a missing resource in kustomization.yaml or a bad patch target, then reproduce locally with flux build kustomization
Ignore it — Flux will fix it on retry
Restart the kustomize-controller pod
Delete the Kustomization and start over

questions.question: Flux applied a commit but the pods are still running the old image. Why?
options: The commit was never pushed to Git
Flux does not deploy container images
Check the applied revision matches the commit, whether the manifest really changed the image, whether a HelmRelease values override pins the old tag, and whether the rollout is stuck on readiness
Kubelet needs a manual restart after every commit

questions.question: The GitRepository fails with an authentication error after a key rotation. How do you fix it?
options: Rebuild the whole cluster
Update the Secret referenced by secretRef with the new key, confirm the public key is registered as a deploy key, check known hosts and reconcile the source
Delete the GitRepository and recreate it without credentials
Disable SSH and use unauthenticated HTTPS

questions.question: A HelmRelease is stuck after a failed upgrade. What do you do?
options: Delete the HelmRelease immediately
Increase the interval to hide the failure
Disable remediation so failures are ignored
Inspect status and events, check the Helm history, fix the values or chart in Git, and if retries are exhausted use reconcile --force or suspend and resume

questions.question: Someone deleted a namespace that Flux manages. What happens and what should you do?
options: If the namespace and its contents are in Git, Flux recreates them on the next reconciliation; data in persistent volumes may be lost, so check backups and tighten RBAC
Nothing happens — Flux never recreates namespaces
Flux deletes the whole cluster
You must run bootstrap again on a new cluster

questions.question: A team removed a directory from Git and production services vanished. How do you prevent this?
options: Set prune: true everywhere to be safe

Pruning did what it was told; prevent repeats with code owners, required reviews on production paths, CI checks that flag large deletions and the kustomize.toolkit.fluxcd.io/prune: disabled annotation on critical objects
Revoke Git access for everyone
Flux should never delete anything under any setting

questions.question: Reconciliation of a large monorepo is slow. How do you speed it up?
options: Set the GitRepository interval to 1s
Disable health checks and pruning
Use sparse checkout or include/ignore rules on the GitRepository, split Kustomizations, raise intervals on stable layers, use Receivers and consider OCI artifacts per environment
Move everything into one Kustomization

questions.question: You need an emergency hotfix outside the normal pipeline. How do you handle it with GitOps?
options: Patch the cluster by hand and leave Git unchanged
Disable Flux permanently
Delete the Kustomization until the incident ends
Commit the fix through an expedited review then reconcile with --with-source; if you must patch live, suspend first, record the change, commit it and resume

questions.question: Image automation commits fail with a permission error. What is wrong?
options: The credential used by ImageUpdateAutomation probably has read-only access (typical for bootstrap deploy keys); give it write access to the target branch and check branch protection rules
The registry token expired
Image automation cannot write to Git at all
The commit message format is invalid

questions.question: Two Kustomizations try to manage the same object. What happens?
options: The last one to reconcile wins permanently
Kubernetes rejects the second Kustomization at admission
They fight — each reconciliation overwrites the other and the object flaps; use flux trace to find both owners and make one Kustomization the only owner
Flux merges both versions automatically

questions.question: A cluster must be rebuilt from scratch after a disaster. How does Flux help?
options: Nothing — Flux state lives only inside the cluster
Create the new cluster, run bootstrap against the same repository path and Flux reapplies everything in dependency order; restore the SOPS key first, and restore data from backups
Run kubectl apply on every manifest by hand
Flux restores persistent volumes from Git

questions.question: Alerts show a Kustomization flipping between Ready and not Ready. How do you investigate?
options: Assume it is a Flux bug and reinstall
Delete the Kustomization and wait
Check the cluster disk space

Look for another actor changing the same objects (an operator, a mutating webhook or a second Kustomization) and for health check timeouts too short for slow-starting pods; flux events and controller logs show which field changes back and forth

questions.question: Explain the pull model. Why does it matter?
options: In a push model CI holds cluster credentials and applies changes; in GitOps an in-cluster controller polls Git and reconciles, so no pipeline holds a kubeconfig with cluster-admin and the blast radius of a leaked CI token shrinks
The pull model means developers pull the repository before editing it
It means images are pulled from a registry at deploy time
It removes the need for a Git repository entirely

questions.question: What is a sync wave in Argo CD and when do you use one?
options: A load-balancing strategy across clusters
The argocd.argoproj.io/sync-wave annotation orders resources inside one sync: lower-numbered waves apply first, each waiting for health before the next
A branch strategy for releasing versions
A way to delay image pulls during rollout

questions.question: How does Argo CD decide if an application is healthy?
options: It only checks that kubectl apply succeeded
It waits for a human to approve the sync

Built-in health checks cover standard types (Deployments, Services, Ingress); custom resources report Progressing or Unknown unless you write a custom Lua health check under resource.customizations in argocd-cm
Health is determined purely by the Git commit status

questions.question: What is App-of-Apps and why not just list every application manually?
options: A tool that generates Helm charts automatically
A single Application that manages one namespace only
A deprecated pattern replaced by sync waves
A parent Application manages child Application manifests, giving one commit to onboard a service, a bootstrap point for a new cluster and a blast-radius boundary

questions.question: Explain Flux's controller architecture
options: Separate controllers each doing one job: source (Git/Helm/OCI artifacts), kustomize (applies overlays), helm (reconciles HelmReleases) and notification (sends alerts)
A single monolithic controller that handles all resource types
Two controllers: one for Git polling and one for the web UI
Controllers are optional plugins installed on top of a core agent

questions.question: How does drift detection actually work?
options: It compares two Git branches on every commit
It uses a webhook from the cluster API to block manual edits
A reconciliation loop compares live cluster state with Git on an interval, and either reports drift or, with self-heal enabled, re-applies the Git version
It only runs when a developer triggers it manually

questions.question: How do you handle secrets in a GitOps repo?
options: Commit encrypted Secrets and let each cluster decrypt them

Never commit plaintext secrets; use Sealed Secrets (cluster-specific key, re-encrypt per cluster), SOPS (encrypt fields with KMS/PGP/age, decrypted at apply time) or External Secrets Operator (pulls at runtime, Git stores only a reference)
Store them in a ConfigMap so they are easy to audit
Put them in the CI pipeline variables only

questions.question: Argo CD vs Flux: what would make you pick one over the other?
options: Argo CD ships a UI, has stronger multi-cluster fan-out from one control plane and centres on the Application resource; Flux is more Unix-philosophy with smaller composable controllers and a lighter footprint — there is no universally correct answer, only a reasoned tradeoff
Flux always wins because it has no UI
Argo CD always wins because it has more controllers
They are functionally identical, so pick by logo
